concepts.title: Magnetic and Non-magnetic Materials
concepts.definition: A magnet attracts some materials and ignores others: iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic, while wood, plastic, glass, cloth and paper are not, so a magnet can sort materials silently.
concepts.key_idea: Attraction is a test: what clings to a magnet is magnetic, the rest is not.

concepts.title: Poles of a Magnet
concepts.definition: The magnetism of a magnet concentrates at its two ends, the poles; a magnet dipped in iron filings shows rings of filings thick at the poles and thin in the middle.
concepts.key_idea: Pull is strongest at the poles: the ends do the work the middle cannot.

why do the ends of a magnet hold more pins

concepts.title: Finding Directions with a Compass
concepts.definition: A freely suspended magnet always settles pointing north-south; this discovery gives the magnetic compass, whose needle lets travellers find directions even without the sun or stars.
concepts.key_idea: The earth itself is a magnet: every compass needle answers to it and shows the way.
question_patterns: how does a magnetic compass find directions

concepts.title: Attraction and Repulsion
concepts.definition: Like poles push apart while unlike poles pull together: north repels north, south repels south, but north attracts south; this rule lets magnets both grip and race each other.
concepts.formula: like poles repel, unlike poles attract
concepts.key_idea: Repulsion is the surest test of a magnet: attraction may be mere iron, but repulsion proves the pole.

why is repulsion the sure test of magnetism
